question: What is Contributory Pension Scheme?
answer_text: Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) is an arrangement where both the employer and the employee contribute a portion of an employee's monthly emolument towards the payment of the employee's pension at retirement.

question: What law established the CPS in Nigeria?
answer_text: The CPS was established in June 2004 by the Pension Reform Act (PRA) 2004, which was repealed and re-enacted in July 2014 (as PRA 2014).

question: How is the CPS different from the Defined Benefits (DB) Pension Scheme?
answer_text: Under the CPS, both the employer and employee contribute certain percentages of the employee's monthly emoluments to build a retirement fund from which benefits are paid at retirement, while under the Defined Benefits (DB) Scheme, total pension obligation is borne by the employer.

question: What is the main objective of CPS?
answer_text: The main objective of the CPS is to ensure that every person that worked in either the public or private sectors in Nigeria, including self-employed persons, receives his/her retirement benefits as and when due.

question: What are the basic features of the CPS?
answer_text: The basic features of the CPS are: I. It is contributory. ii. It is fully funded. iii. It is based on individualized RSA. iv. Pension funds are privately managed and held in custody by Pension Fund Administrators (PFAs) and Pension Fund Custodians (PFCs), respectively. v. There is provision of Group Life Insurance Policy cover for employees.

question: What is a Retirement Savings Account (RSA)?
answer_text: An RSA is an account opened by an employee with a PFA of his/her choice, into which all pension contributions are remitted and invested for the purpose of paying retirement/terminal benefits.

question: What constitutes monthly emoluments?
answer_text: The constituent of monthly emoluments is as may be defined in the employee's contract of employment, but should not be less than the total sum of basic salary, housing and transport allowances.

question: Does the RSA operate like a Bank Account?
answer_text: Unlike a bank account that can be accessed at will by the account holder, the RSA can only be accessed: a) at retirement; or b) if an employee disengages or is disengaged from employment: i) on the advice of a suitably qualified physician or properly constituted medical board certifying that the employee is no longer mentally or physically capable of carrying out the functions of his office, or ii) due to total or permanent disability of the mind or body; or iii) before the age of 50 years and is unable to secure another employment after four months of disengagement; or c) in the event of death.

question: What is the role of the National Pension Commission (PenCom)?
answer_text: PenCom is the regulator and supervisor of all pension matters in Nigeria. It licenses all pension operators, issues regulations, guidelines and ensures effective administration of all pension schemes in Nigeria.

question: What is a Pension Fund Administrator (PFA)?
answer_text: A PFA is a company licensed by PenCom for the sole purpose of managing and administering pension and other retirement benefit schemes' assets. Some of the PFAs are licensed to manage and administer retirement benefit schemes for staff of organizations that had existing pension schemes prior to the commencement of the CPS in 2004. These companies are called Closed Pension Fund Administrators (CPFAs).

question: What is a Pension Fund Custodian (PFC)?
answer_text: A PFC is a company licensed by PenCom for the sole purpose of holding all pension funds and assets on trust for employees, as well as beneficiaries of the RSA and other retirement benefit schemes.

question: Who is mandatorily covered by the CPS?
answer_text: The CPS covers employees in the public service of the Federation, Federal Capital Territory, States, Local Governments and private sector organizations with 3 or more employees.

question: Can employees who are not mandatorily covered in the PRA participate in the CPS?
answer_text: Yes, employees of organizations with less than 3 employees, as well as self-employed persons may voluntarily participate in the CPS under the Micro Pension Plan.

question: Who is exempted from the CPS?
answer_text: Judicial Officers, members of the Armed Forces, the Intelligence and Secret Services of the Federation; retirees under any pension scheme existing before 30 June 2004; and employees who had 3 or less years to retire as at 30 June 2004.

question: Can foreigners employed in Nigeria participate in the CPS?
answer_text: Foreigners working in Nigeria are not mandated by law to participate in the CPS. However, such foreigners may voluntarily participate in the Scheme.

question: Can Nigerians working abroad participate in the CPS?
answer_text: Nigerian citizens working abroad are not mandated by law to participate in the CPS.

question: What happens to the RSA of a person who resigns from an organization in Nigeria and takes up appointment outside Nigeria?
answer_text: Any person who resigns from an organization in Nigeria and takes up appointment outside Nigeria is entitled to decide with the new employer to continue remitting his pension contributions into his/her RSA in Nigeria. However, if the person chooses to discontinue with the scheme in Nigeria or the new employer has an entirely different pension arrangement, he/she may access his RSA upon retirement or attaining the age of 50 years, whichever is earlier.

question: Can employees on temporary, contract or tenured appointments join the CPS?
answer_text: Employees on temporary, contract or tenured appointments may voluntarily join the CPS.

question: Can a retiree under the DB Scheme participate in the CPS?
answer_text: A retiree under the DB Scheme can voluntarily participate in the CPS if he/she secures a new employment.

question: How can an employee open an RSA?
answer_text: An employee should approach a PFA of his/her choice, complete the RSA registration form and provide the following supporting documents: i. Letter of Employment or Attestation Letter (in the case of Police Personnel). ii. Valid means of identification (Staff ID Card; National Driver's Licence; Permanent Voter's Card; National Identity Card or International Passport). iii. Enrolment Slip issued by the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) indicating the National Identity Number (NIN). The PFA would process the request for RSA registration and issue a unique Personal Identification Number (PIN).

question: Can an employee have more than one RSA?
answer_text: An employee is required by law to open only one RSA, which should be maintained throughout his/her lifetime even if he/she changes employment, transfers his/her RSA to another PFA or retires.

question: What would happen where an employee fails to open an RSA, six months after assumption of duty?
answer_text: The employer shall request a PFA to open a nominal (temporary) RSA, into which the employee's monthly pension contributions shall be remitted pending when the employee regularizes the RSA.

question: What should be done when pension deductions are not remitted by employers?
answer_text: Where an employer fails in its statutory responsibility to remit the pension contributions of its employees, the concerned employee(s) should complain directly to PenCom. The name and address of the defaulting employer should be provided to enable PenCom engage the employer without compromising the confidentiality of the complainant.

question: How does PenCom assist contributors to recover unremitted pension contributions from their employers?
answer_text: PenCom engages the services of Recovery Agents to recover outstanding pension liabilities. Where this fails, PenCom institutes legal action against the defaulting employer.

question: What are the implications of an employee having more than one RSA?
answer_text: An employee with more than one RSA may suffer incorrect remittances into the valid RSA and loss of investment income that would have accrued over the period. Such employee may also experience loss of time on multiple RSA reconciliation and difficulty in accessing benefits.

question: Can an employer or a Union compel its workers or members to open RSAs with a particular PFA?
answer_text: It is illegal for an employer or a Union to compel its employees or members to open RSAs with a particular PFA. The choice of a PFA for opening an RSA is the exclusive right of an employee or a member of a Union.

question: What should I do if I have more than one RSA?
answer_text: You are required to present all your RSA PINs to any of the PFAs that issued them. The PFA would recapture your details including one of the registered PINs. The recaptured PIN becomes your PIN for life, while all other RSA PINs will be forwarded to PenCom for deactivation after reconciling the balances (if any) in the RSAs associated with them.

question: Do I need to be recaptured even if I have only one RSA?
answer_text: Yes. All existing RSA holders (Active & Retiree) who registered before 1 July 2019, must participate in the Data Recapture Exercise to update their RSA registration records.

question: What is the implication of not participating in the data recapture exercise?
answer_text: The implications of not participating in the Data Recapture Exercise include: i. Inability to access retirement benefits at retirement. ii. Non-resolution of multiple RSA registrations. iii. Reconciliation of multiple registration of RSAs with balances will be hampered. iv. Inability of RSA holders to update registration records in the future. v. Inability to transfer RSA from current PFA to another PFA.

question: what are conventional assets according to Pencom?
answer_text: Assets/Securities/Instruments that are not based on Islamic shari’ah principles

question: What should the pension company do in order for me to get my pension money early?
answer_text: LPFOs shall explain to consumers the eligibility and prerequisite requirements for other grounds of benefits payment or for accessing RSA balance (Temporary access to 25%, Residential Mortgage, Voluntary Contribution, Death Benefit, Pre-Act benefits and NSITF contribution).

question: What is the Financial Regulation Advisory Council of Experts?
answer_text: An advisory body on Islamic Banking and Finance established by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to advice on matters relating to Islamic commercial jurisprudence for the effective regulation and supervision of Non- Interest Financial Institutions and products in Nigeria.

question: What happens to my pension after I change my name?
answer_text: In the case of existing RSA holders who changed their names after their RSA registration and obtained NINs with their new names, PFAs shall recapture such individuals using the names on the CRS. To support the change of name, PFAs shall upload to ECRS, the documents listed in Section 5.2.15 (1).

question: How does my pension company handle my private data?
answer_text: PFAs shall abide by the Code of Ethics on Business Practices issued by the Commission, and shall respect the confidentiality of sensitive information relating to their contributors.

question: What happens if my pension company submitted the wrong information to PenCom?
answer_text: Any PFA that negligently submits to the Commission, a request with incorrect information and later request the permission of the Commission to resubmit the request, shall pay an administrative sanction of N100,000.00 per RSA.

question: Who actually holds my pension money?
answer_text: PFAs shall maintain the Pension Fund Custodian (PFC) that manages the custody of the ‘Active’ RSA Funds (Fund I, II and III) to administer the custodial services of the ‘Active’ and Retiree RSA Fund VI. Operational Framework For Non-Interest Fund (Fund VI) Page 15 of 21

question: Do pension laws apply to me as a local government worker?
answer_text: The provisions of the Pension Reform Act 2014 (PRA 2014) applies to all employees in the Public Service of the Federation, Federal Capital Territory, States and Local Governments and the Private Sector Organizations in which there are three or more employees. However, Section 2(3) of the Act provides that employees of organizations with less than three employees as well as self-employed persons shall be entitled to participate under the Contributory Pension Scheme in accordance with Guidelines issued by the Commission. The categories of persons referred to in Section 2(3) of the PRA 2014 constitute the vast majority of the working population.

question: A PFA agent told me my current pension company is bad and will lose my money, so I should move to them. Are they even allowed to talk like that?
answer_text: It should be noted that encouraging a free market environment is vital to enhance effective service delivery for consumers. Therefore, Pension Fund Operators should actively promote healthy competition while refraining from unethical and de-marketing practices, ensuring fair and beneficial outcomes for all consumers.

question: I saw a pension company advert on TV promising my money will double fast. Are they allowed to promise things like that?
answer_text: The Commission shall ensure that advertisements by Pension Fund Operators aligns with approved product features. Accordingly, Pension Fund Operators shall ensure that advertisements on pension products/ services shall: i. Not be misleading; ii. Be clear and explicit; iii. State the features of the products/services; and iv. Neither misrepresent nor exaggerate the benefits of the products/services.

question: I just lost my job and want to know my options for my pension money. Is the pension company supposed to tell me?
answer_text: LPFOs shall provide clear and concise information about benefits computation and exit options.

question: I work for the state government. Does my state have to show its pension law to PenCom?
answer_text: Yes. States are advised to forward their State Pension Bill and Laws to PenCom for review and input before and after signing. This will reduce anomalies and inconsistencies with the PRA 2014.

question: My state owes me pension for the years I already worked. Where does the state keep the money to pay that?
answer_text: A State can open an RBBRF account for the payment of Accrued Rights with the Central Bank of Nigeria or a PFA of its choice.

question: I retired last year and stopped getting my pension statements. What should I do on my side to keep receiving them?
answer_text: PFAs are mandated by PenCom to issue RSA statements to contributors and retirees at least once every three months. RSA holders are expected to update their contact details with their PFAs, from time to time, to ensure that they receive the RSA Statements regularly.

question: I just got my first job. Can I pick any pension company I want, or does my boss choose for me?
answer_text: Employees are at liberty to open an RSA with any PFA of their choice. However, there are exceptions where a State has an arrangement to select a pool of PFAs within the State to manage its pension fund assets.

question: My company has its own pension company just for its staff. Can I move my pension to a different one I like?
answer_text: Every employee may decide to join the contributory pension scheme or move his RSA from a closed PFA to a PFA of his choice subject to such rules and regulations as may be issued by the National Pension Commission. CAN A SUBSIDIARY COMPANY APPLY AS A CLOSED PFA A subsidiary of any company may apply for licence to operate as a Closed PFA provided it satisfies the requirements of the Pension Reform Act 2014.

question: Can my pension company take the money in my account and use it for its own business?
answer_text: The Pension Fund Administrator cannot collect or spend the pension money in the RSA. WHO IS A “CLOSED PENSION FUND ADMINISTRATOR (CPFA)?” Any employer managing its existing pension scheme before the enactment of the Pension Reform Act 2014 may apply to the National Pension Commission to be licenced as a Closed Pension Fund Administrator to continue to manage such pension scheme. A closed PFA cannot open or manage RSA for employees other than its employees or employees of its parent company if it is a subsidiary.

question: I’m a market trader. Is this micro pension thing not just the same as saving my money in the bank?
answer_text: Yes. MPP is different from savings account maintained with a commercial bank because any savings made under the Plan can only be withdrawn as monthly pension after retirement, except the Contingent portion of the contribution.

question: My pension account is just like a bank account, abi? Can I collect my money from it whenever I want?
answer_text: The RSA is similar to a bank account with the exception that a contributor cannot withdraw money from the RSA before his/her retirement. The PFA is required to invest the money and issue statements of account at least once in every quarter to the contributor.

question: When I get my pension statement, what things should I see on it?
answer_text: The RSA statement has minimum information and disclosure requirements mandated by PenCom, which include amount contributed from inception to date, monthly employer and employee pension contributions, income earned (returns on Investment), and total RSA balance as at the period. PFAs also send RSA balances via text message. In addition, the RSA holder has the option of checking the performance of his RSA online and on digital platforms or physically visiting the nearest branch of his/her PFA to obtain a hard copy of the RSA statement.

question: New worker here. Will I pay anything to the company keeping my pension?
answer_text: The PFA will charge fees for the services being rendered on the RSA subject to such guidelines as may be issued by the National Pension Commission from time to time.

question: I’m a casual worker, not permanent staff. Should my boss still be paying into my pension?
answer_text: The PRA 2014 has not categorized workers on permanent or casual basis. Employers are mandated to remit pension contribution of every worker on its payroll. For staff whose salaries are not broken into basic, transport and housing allowances, the pension contributions should be based on the salary payable.

question: Can my state’s pension fund be used to pay life insurance for workers?
answer_text: Yes. States can have special funds arrangement for their employees and also an RBBRF account, as long as it covers for the payment of pension contributions, outstanding pension liabilities as a result of unpaid contributions and accrued pension rights and group life insurance purpose.

question: How much is my boss supposed to put into my pension every month?
answer_text: The employer shall contribute a minimum of 10% of the employee’s monthly emolument (sumation of monthly basic salary, transport and housing allowance) towards the retirement benefits of the employee.

question: I’m a tailor on micro pension and I need some money urgently. Can I take some out before I retire?
answer_text: A Micro Pension Contributor can withdraw an amount from his/her contingent portion by applying to his/her PFA in a prescribed format.

question: My father is retiring and someone told him about “annuity”, what is that?
answer_text: Annuity is a method of receiving pension by a retiree through a contract purchased from an approved Life Insurance Company. It provides a guaranteed periodic income (pension) to a retiree throughout his/her life after retirement.

question: I’m not happy with my pension company. Can I move my pension to another one?
answer_text: Yes. However, an RSA holder is only allowed to transfer his/her RSA once in every 365 days (12 calendar months), as stipulated in Section 13 of the PRA 2014.

question: I’m a market woman on micro pension. How do I pay my money in, can I just bring cash?
answer_text: Contributions under the MPP can be made by cash deposit or electronic transfer through any payment platform, or other financial service agents approved by CBN.

question: My company says it wants to manage our pensions itself instead of using a pension company. Is that allowed?
answer_text: Any employer having existing pension fund assets worth N500,000,000 or more who also meets the requirements of the Pension Reform Act 2014,may apply to the National Pension Commission for a closed PFA licence to enable it manage the pension funds of its employees directly or through its subsidiary.

question: I’m leaving my bank job to join a telecom company. Will changing jobs mess up my pension?
answer_text: Movement from one employment to another does not affect pension under the new scheme. The reform has removed the bottlenecks associated with the transfer of service from one organisation or sector to another, especially with regard to qualification for pension and the sharing formula for payment of pension as between employers. However, contributors are advised to update their personal and employer details with their PFA regularly to ensure that they receive updated correspondence.

question: I’m retiring from my provision shop and I’m on micro pension. What is this “programmed withdrawal” they keep mentioning?
answer_text: Programmed Withdrawal is a mode of benefits withdrawal by which a Micro Pension retiree receives pension through his PFA on a periodic basis, i.e. monthly or quarterly.

question: I retired from the civil service last year. Can I now join micro pension to save more?
answer_text: No. Retirees from the Formal Sector cannot participate in the MPP. MPP allows participation by the self-employed and person working in organizations with less than 3 employees.

question: Can my pension company use my money to buy its own company shares?
answer_text: No. A PFA is prohibited from investing pension fund assets in the shares or any other securities issued by itself or its PFC and also in investing in shares or any other securities issued by a shareholder or related party of the PFA or its PFC.

question: My pension statement mentions “unit price”. What does that even mean?
answer_text: Unit price is a measure of the value of the fund in which your contributions is a part of. It represents the fund price as at the day your contributions is credited into your Retirement Savings Account.

question: I have shares in two pension companies. Is there a limit to how much I can own in both?
answer_text: Where an individual or institution owns shares in more than one PFA or PFC, he/she cannot have significant shareholding (5% and above) in more than one PFA or PFC.

question: PenCom approved my pension payment, but my pension company paid me less than that. What happens now?
answer_text: Any PFA that pays an amount lower than that specified on the no-objection approval granted by the Commission, shall, in addition to paying the differential to the retiree, pay an administrative sanction of N500,000.00.

question: I opened my pension account two weeks ago and nothing has come. How long should it take to get my registration letter?
answer_text: PFAs shall issue their clients with letters of registration within 5 working days of opening of the RSAs. Such letters shall contain, in the minimum, Name of the RSA Holder, RSA Holder’s Address, PFA Name, PIN, Date of Registration, RSA Holder’s Mobile Number and Employer’s Name (where applicable).

question: My pension company called me a “prospective retiree”. What does that mean?
answer_text: Prospective Retirees: An employee with contributions in RSA Fund III (above 50 years) who is making preparations for retirement from active service or has applied for retirement benefits.

question: My pension company sent wrong details about me to PenCom, and now my pension money is finishing too fast. Is there any punishment for them?
answer_text: Any PFA that negligently submits to the Commission, a request with incorrect information that is likely to result to accelerated depletion of the RSA balance of a retiree, shall pay an administrative sanction of N500,000.00. In addition, the PFA shall refund to the RSA both the amount that was overpaid and the lost investment income.

question: My company registered me for pension when I joined. How will I get proof that I’m registered?
answer_text: In the case of registrations initiated by employers, PFAs shall issue evidence of registration to employees through their employers within 5 working days of receipt of their Temporary PINs from the Commission. Such letters shall contain Name of the Employee, PFA Name, Temporary PIN, Employer Name and Employer Address.

question: PenCom has approved my retirement money, but my pension company is still not paying me. Is there any punishment for them?
answer_text: Where a PFA delays payment of retirement benefits for up to 5 working days after receipt of no-objection from the Commission, it shall pay an administrative sanction of N200,000.00 and N20,000.00 for every day of delay thereafter. Revised Regulation on the Administration of Retirement and Terminal Benefits Page 36 of 60 Public

question: Is there a limit to how much extra money I can add to my pension account on my own?
A pension advert said I will get 15% return. What return should I really expect from my pension?
Who can see my details once my pension company sends them to the national database?
Will my pension company charge me to update my phone number and address?
Can I register for my pension account online from my phone, or must I go to the office?
What are the actual targets of Nigeria’s financial inclusion plan?
Does Fund VI pay lower returns than the normal pension funds?
How do I start paying extra money into my pension on my own?
What phone number or email can I use to reach PenCom about this?
I’m retired and some old unpaid pension money just entered my account. How long will my pension company take to recalculate my monthly pension?
Once I ask to switch pension companies, how long does the move take?
Will my pension PIN change after I move to a new pension company?
I’m on annuity and not happy with my insurance company. Can I move to a different insurance company?
At what age will I retire under this pension scheme?
answer_text: Retirement age under the CPS depends on each employee’s terms and conditions of employment.

question: I retired, but I just got a new job. Can I pause my monthly pension while I’m working again?
answer_text: Where a retiree on PW secures employment, he/she may request the suspension of his/her monthly pension in writing and by filling a consent form. When the retiree decides to resume collecting his/her monthly pension, he/she shall request in writing. The pension would be determined by reprogramming the current RSA balance using the retiree's current age. In such circumstances there shall be no pension arrears.

question: My HR manager is telling all of us to move our pensions to one particular company. Can they force me?
answer_text: No, it is not permissible for an employer to compel its employees to transfer their RSAs to any particular PFA. The decision to transfer an RSA, similar to that of selecting a PFA in the first instance, is the exclusive preserve of the employee. Page 5 of 7

question: I’ve been collecting the same pension amount for years. Will it ever go up?
answer_text: There shall be a periodic pension enhancement for retirees on PW based on the Return of Investment of funds in the RSA and PenCom's directive (currently – after every 3 years).

question: If I choose annuity when I retire, can I collect some of my money at once first?
answer_text: A retiree can procure a Life Annuity Provisional Agreement using the RSA balance after accessing a portion as lump sum (by choice), and the balance as premium from an insurance company, which in turn provides the monthly/quarterly payments (Annuity). The RLA product is subject to the Regulations jointly issued by PenCom and NAICOM.

question: Does my pension company need any documents from me before it can register me?
answer_text: PFAs must obtain the minimum documents specified by the Commission in Sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.3 and 5.3.9 of these Guidelines to register an individual and shall obtain the minimum documents specified by the Commission within a period not exceeding six (6) months for recaptured RSA holders.

question: I’ve had my pension account for years and they want me to redo my registration. Do I need the same documents as someone opening a new account?
answer_text: Except as otherwise stated in Section 5.3 of these Guidelines, all data and documentation requirements applicable to New RSA registrations outlined in these Guidelines, shall also be applicable to Existing Contributor Recapture.

question: I stopped working last year and no money goes into my pension now. Am I still an active contributor?
answer_text: Active RSA contributors: Employees in active service who is making periodic pension contributions to his registered Retirement Savings Account (RSA) in Funds I,II or III with a licensed PFA.

question: I’m a Muslim worried about my pension being invested the halal way. Who advises PenCom on Islamic finance?
answer_text: The FRACE shall serve as an advisory body to the Commission on Islamic Finance matters and specifically on all subsidiary legislations on investment of Fund VI assets.

question: A pension agent wants to register me again even though I already have an account. Is that allowed?
answer_text: PFAs shall open a single RSA for an individual and where ECRS notifies any PFA of the existence of a contributor on the database, the PFA shall not attempt to re-register that individual. The Commission shall deem such attempt by any PFA to re-register an individual as fraudulent and shall issue appropriate sanctions as outlined in Section 6.0 of these Guidelines.
